userVisible: The module builds into one executable file that needs only Node.
A caller can discover every command and whether it reads or writes data.
Startup checks report runtime, binary checksum, database integrity and migrations.
Creating a task can be retried without creating duplicate work.
Task details can be changed while retries preserve the original answer.
Finished work changes status only through an explicit reopen.
Adding a prerequisite refuses cycles and missing tasks.
Removing a prerequisite makes the newly available work visible.
A caller can retrieve one existing task and recognize a missing task.
A caller can filter tasks by list, status and label.
Importing a work list twice is unchanged, and invalid imports store nothing.
Next work has completed prerequisites and a repeatable explained ordering.
The task graph reports dependencies, estimated effort and the critical path.
Board data groups every task into its current status.
Task history records edits, actors and status notes in order.
Rebuilding task tables from history preserves the current work and dependencies.
Read-only metrics measure waiting, cycle time and throughput from history.
Seeded simulations compare finish dates without changing stored tasks.
Read-only scheduling respects dependencies, availability and capacity.
An independent checker reports conflicting assignments without changing tasks.
The module follows the shared JSON, exit-code, deterministic and read-only contract.
Repository documentation and examples can be understood without private context.
The lifecycle model passes and deliberately broken variants fail their named invariants.
